items.title: Al Wynn Interview, 1958-05-29
items.q: he had a marching band, a brass band around there. So he'd always put me on the trombone and he would play the trumpet.

ctx.x: And just as good as he was on trombone. That's just as sad as he was on trumpet to my idea of thinking. His ideas on trumpet were very corny. I mean, my way of thinking. And he loved the trumpet. The trumpet was really his love. And after I got so that I could play, he had a marching band, a brass band around there. So he'd always put me on the trombone and he would play the trumpet. And I just didn't like his trumpet playing at all. It was really ratatirous, you know. But he had a terrific pair of lips. I mean,…

You know, Jolly Roe Martin and his Library of Congress records, he did a lot of talking and playing and, too. And he said Roy was his favorite trombonist. He said he was the greatest they had in New Orleans in the old days, too.
